_comment: Every public claim on monogate.org that a Lean theorem is proved, pinned to the artifact that proves it. `npm run predeploy` runs ../../monogate-lean/tools/lean_claims/check_claims.py over it: each claimed theorem must be declared in its file at the pinned revision; the file must compile in its environment, with the toolchain, package revisions and local-import sources exactly as pinned; each theorem's own #print axioms must have no sorryAx and nothing outside allowed_axioms (the footprint observed on the day the claim was added); and every label occurrence in src/ and public/ must be a site below or an exemption with its reason. To make a claim, add it here in the same change as the page text. scripts/check_proofs_page.py reads the monogate-lean pin from `sources`. The labels are the Lean-verified / machine-checked family, "sorryAx-free" (with or without backticks), and since 2026-09-13 the bare words "proved" and "proven" in any case (\bproved\b, \bproven\b), which subsume the earlier "is proved", "are proved", "proved theorem", PROVED and Proved labels; "unproved" and "improved" do not match. /proofs/apollonius renders PROVED badges from src/data/apollonius-evidence.json; scripts/check-exhibit-gates.mjs fails unless every theorem those badges cite is registered here. A theorem name containing a prime (e.g. MachLib.Real.quadratic_lyapunov_sublevel_tight') cannot be registered: check_claims.py's report parser reads names between single quotes.
